原句.原句: Strong Li+ solvation and strong LiPS solvation in DOL/DME trigger poor sulfur reversibility and severe Li anode degradation, resulting in quick capacity fading after only 55 cycles.
This corresponds to the decoupled impacts of long-chain LiPS corrosion and low CE due to the poor Li SEI.
This indicates the liquid−solid oxidation on stage V becomes unfavorable with strong LiPS solvation.
In other words, the concentration of long-chain LiPS preserved in the DOL/DME electrolyte is significant even at the end of charge, which agrees with the previous reports.

原句.原句: On the other hand, the smaller SEI resistance (RSEI) in DOL/F4DEE and DOL/TTE than DOL/DME indicates the benefit of weakened Li+ and LiPS solvation on Li anode.
These results demonstrate the correlation between moderate Li+ solvation and improved Li stripping/plating reversibility in DOL/F4DEE, which aligns well with previous studies on the Li metal anode.
The weak‖LiPS solvation also suppresses parasitic corrosion reactions on the Li metal (Note S4).

原句.原句: On the other hand, Li||CP GITT shows similar overpotential across various LiPS solvations (Figure S20a).
Again, the similar overpotential across three electrolytes validates the noncorrelation between LiPS solvation and LiPS oxidation kinetics (Figure S20b).
These results unravel that the LiPS chain-shortening process with weak LiPS solvation relies more on short-chain LiPS (liquid−solid) reduction than long-chain LiPS (liquid−liquid) reduction.

It is reported that electrolytes with weaker LiPS solvation shift LiPS disproportionation equilibrium toward the formation of shorter-chain LiPS species that deliver lower specific capacity during the reduction on stage II.
Thus, the capacity difference in these electrolytes is mainly attributed to LiPS conversion thermodynamics rather than kinetics.
In this regard, our results‖differ from the conventional concepts, wherein electrolytes with weak LiPS solvation are often challenged by their poor redox kinetics.
